title: CUDA out-of-memory error loading OPT-125M with vLLM under WSL2
body: I successfully installed vLLM in WSL2, but the sample code fails while initializing `LLM` with a local `facebook_opt-125m` model. It reports `# GPU blocks: 37375, # CPU blocks: 7281`, then raises `RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory` from `cache_engine.py` while `allocate_cpu_cache()` calls `torch.empty`. I am using Python 3.10.11, an RTX 3090 with 24 GB, and Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS under WSL2. Can anyone help?

symptoms_visible: When I initialize vLLM with OPT-125M under WSL2, startup reports 37375 GPU blocks and 7281 CPU blocks, then `allocate_cpu_cache()` raises `RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory`.
N0.label: N0 small model fails during cache initialization

symptoms_visible: With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.50`, vLLM reports 19899 GPU blocks and 7281 CPU blocks but still raises the CUDA out-of-memory error from `allocate_cpu_cache()`.
The same local OPT-125M model loads successfully in text-generation-webui.
N1.label: N1 utilization and synchronous-launch probe completed

symptoms_visible: OPT-125M works through text-generation-webui, while vLLM still fails during cache initialization.
I see the same vLLM OOM on another WSL2 machine with small models including OPT-125M and Pythia-70M, even though standard Transformers can run them.
N2.label: N2 model-specific failure ruled out

symptoms_visible: Nothing else is using my GPU before the run; GPU activity and VRAM spike only while vLLM tries to load the model, and then initialization crashes.
The other affected WSL2 machine also has no competing GPU workload and shows the same load-time spike and crash.
N3.label: N3 external GPU contention ruled out

symptoms_visible: After disabling `pin_memory` for the CPU cache allocation, vLLM initializes OPT-125M under WSL2 without the previous CUDA out-of-memory error.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with WSL pin-memory workaround

question_patterns: Can you retry with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.80` or lower and report the result?
Please set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, rerun the sample, and paste the resulting traceback.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and used `gpu_memory_utilization=0.50`. It now reports 19899 GPU blocks and 7281 CPU blocks, but the error is otherwise the same: `allocate_cpu_cache()` reaches `torch.empty` and raises `RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory`. Text-generation-webui can load my model successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With `gpu_memory_utilization=0.50`, vLLM initializes and generates text normally.
The same error occurs with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.60` instead of 0.50, and the reported GPU block count is slightly different.

edges.comment: Real thread c0-c1: lowering the utilization and enabling synchronous CUDA error reporting were handler-initiated probes. The reporter supplied the resulting block count and traceback; the unchanged failure remains raw observation rather than a diagnosis.

question_patterns: Can you test the standard `facebook/opt-125m` model to make sure the local model is not the problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I can load `facebook/opt-125m` in text-generation-webui and use it successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, `facebook/opt-125m` also fails to load in text-generation-webui and standard Transformers.

edges.comment: Real thread c2-c4. A second affected WSL2 user also volunteered that OPT-125M and Pythia-70M fail in vLLM while both work with standard Transformers; that multi-user evidence is folded into the target node's volunteered information.

question_patterns: Can you check whether another process is using GPU memory before vLLM starts?
What does GPU and VRAM usage look like immediately before and during initialization?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm pretty sure no other process is using my GPU. Before the run it is idle; while the code tries to load the model, both GPU activity and VRAM suddenly spike, and then it crashes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Another process is already consuming almost all 24 GB of VRAM before I start vLLM.
The GPU is idle before the run and the same load-time spike occurs, but Windows Task Manager labels the activity as Compute rather than 3D.

edges.comment: Real thread c6, c9-c10. The reporter described the GPU graph, but no provided local attachment is available, so the remote screenshot is not referenced. A second affected WSL2 user confirmed the same no-contention behavior and is folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Treat the misleading CUDA OOM as a WSL pinned-host-memory limit hit while vLLM allocates its CPU cache; temporarily disable pinned memory for that allocation and have the user rerun the sample to verify initialization.
solution.concrete_example: In `vllm/worker/cache_engine.py`, find the `torch.empty` allocations used by `allocate_cpu_cache()` and remove or comment out `pin_memory=True`. Then rerun the original OPT-125M sample and confirm that `LLM` initializes and generates output without the OOM.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the WSL environment, cache-allocation traceback, utilization probe, successful non-vLLM model load, and idle-GPU observation. Identifying WSL's limited `pin_memory` support—apparently capped around 2 GB in this environment—as the reason the CPU cache allocation surfaces a CUDA OOM was the maintainers' conclusion from pair-debugging, not a fact stated by the reporter before the fix.

edges.comment: Resolution from c12-c14: pair-debugging isolated WSL pinned-memory behavior. The temporary source-level workaround was to comment out `pin_memory=True` in the CPU-cache allocations; the reporter thanked the maintainer and closed the issue. Later comments about unrelated Linux configurations, larger models, quantization, sequence length, and utilization tuning are outside this original resolved case.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original case's root cause as WSL's pinned host-memory limitation being hit by vLLM's `pin_memory=True` CPU-cache allocation, with the CUDA OOM message being misleading rather than evidence that OPT-125M exhausted the RTX 3090's VRAM.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the traceback reaches `allocate_cpu_cache()` and `torch.empty`, lowering `gpu_memory_utilization` changes the GPU block count but not the failure, the model works in another runtime, and no competing process is using the GPU.
Must recommend removing or commenting out `pin_memory=True` in the CPU-cache allocation in `vllm/worker/cache_engine.py` as the temporary fix for this WSL2 case.

Must not present lowering `gpu_memory_utilization`, setting `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, changing the model, or merely closing other GPU processes as the resolution; those directions did not eliminate the reported failure or were ruled out by collected evidence.
Must ask the user to rerun the original sample after disabling pinned memory and verify successful initialization before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Python and local-LLM user who can install vLLM under WSL2, edit a sample script, set environment variables, change constructor arguments, inspect GPU usage, and modify an installed Python source file with guidance.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise and cooperative; pastes complete tracebacks, reports exact parameter changes and block counts, and answers direct diagnostic questions without independently asserting a root cause.
